record: Re-execution of the submitted inference and reconstruction of the training frame cache on the original server
note: The server clock runs in UTC; every timestamp below is UTC except where marked. The 20261028 date in this file name is the Asia/Shanghai date.

gpu_model_load.how: code/infer.py loaded the public base with AutoModelForImageTextToText (BF16, sdpa) and applied the delivered LoRA adapter through PeftModel.from_pretrained; the journal records the adapter SHA-256 of every row

settings.frame_sampling: min(32, floor(total_frames/2)*2) frames decoded per video, max_pixels=262144, video_fps=2.0

comparison_to_submitted_run.conclusion: All three inference artifacts were reproduced exactly on the original server with the delivered code, adapter, base weight and videos.

frame_cache_reconstruction.result: Every reconstructed .npy matched the frozen cache manifest in both byte count and SHA-256; the rebuilt training/train.json points at the reconstructed cache.
frame_cache_reconstruction.short_video_note: The archived helper requests a fixed 16 training frames. Source videos shorter than 16 frames decode at the largest even frame count available, because qwen_vl_utils rounds an explicit odd nframes to the next multiple of 2 and would raise instead of clamping. internet_0038 (15 frames, decoded at 14) is the only odd case; preparation of that single video at 14 frames reproduced its frozen .npy byte-for-byte.

first_attempt.reason: internet_0038.mp4 has 15 frames; the fixed 16-frame request raised ValueError: nframes should in interval [2, 15], but got 16, and the historical fallback re-requested an odd 15 frames, which was rounded back to 16
first_attempt.disposition: verification/prepare_runtime.py now sets the frame count per video and supports reusing an interrupted cache directory; the 531 files written by the first attempt were re-verified by SHA-256 and reused

not_performed: The one-epoch LoRA continuation was not re-executed. Its training command was staged and printed by prepare_runtime.py, but retraining would not be bit-identical on GPU and would take about 2 h 49 min.
No submission, upload or external publication was performed during this verification.
limitations: Exact reproduction was obtained on the same host and library versions as the original run; a different GPU, driver or library set may change BF16 kernel results.
Training reproducibility is supported by the frozen plan, receipts and a fully reconstructed frame cache, not by a new training run.
